⚠ The provenance sentence that stood here was false, and the divergence it hid is 21 % (measured 2026-09-05, qou-i229). It read: "Values are the displayed digits of the 50-dps witness q-beta-spectral-bridge.witness.json, regenerated from the canonical CAL-2 pinning q-pinning-50-digit.witness.json." The witness contains none of these values and declares q0Anchor: proton, not the canonical CAL-2 (muon) pinning.

q_0 1.109978595557335 1.1099785827513808\ldots (proton)
z 0.4993203340335613 0.6126880371464652\ldots
\ln(1+zh) 0.09929139859972778 0.1205248238414840\ldots
predicted bridge 1.897907634269324 1.5660730493910099\ldots

Each side reproduces its own numbers exactly, so this is two different computations, not drift: the bridge ratio differs by 21.2\,\%.

Which side is stale: the table, not the producer. An earlier version of this note said the producer had drifted from the stated definition. That is backwards and withdrawn. The proposition's z = 1/(\sqrt q + 1/\sqrt q) is convention C, excised by the owner ruling of 2026-08-09; the producer's q^3/(q^2+1) is convention D, which the registry records as the definitional convention for qbeta-decay per the ruling of 2026-08-15. So the producer moved to the ruled convention and the proposition was left behind — the ordinary C→D content lag, not its inverse. Migration tracked as qou-cds1.

The table does faithfully follow its proposition: prop:q-beta-spectral-bridge defines z := 1/(\sqrt q + 1/\sqrt q), which is what these values use; q_beta_spectral_bridge_witness.py computes q^3/(q^2+1) instead — and stores it under the field name z_markov_jones, while the proposition calls its z "the Markov–Jones parameter". The same name for two formulas is what hid this, and both of the witness's assertions PASS, because a producer checking itself against itself cannot see that it has drifted from the block it names in contentBlock.

Which z is right is an authoring question and is not settled here; the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta figures differ by \sim 0.05 MeV between the two readings. Nothing in this table, the proposition or the producer has been changed — only this sentence, which was false under either reading. the_qbeta_bridge_table_and_its_witness_compute_different_z_probe.py.

⚠ Retraction (2026-09-05). A caveat here said h^2 = 0.04370621823290131 "carries a retired q_0" and that this table was internally inconsistent. Both are withdrawn. h^2 is exactly (h)^2 as published — they agree to 9.0\times10^{-18} — and every value in the table reproduces from the quoted q_0 with the proposition's own z. The earlier claim came from matching h^2 against closed forms at three candidate pins, where the significant-figure bucketing was too coarse to separate them. The table is self-consistent; what is not is its relationship to the producer, above.
